source.work: MDN Web Docs, setTimeout and setInterval
source.paraphrase: Passing a string to a timer compiles it as code when the timer fires. The string runs with the caller's privileges like eval.

invariants.why: A string that reaches a timer becomes code with full access, so any injection in the string is an injection in the program.
invariants.fixHint: Pass an arrow function or a function reference instead of the code as a string.
invariants.avoid: A template literal without placeholders is still a string argument and still compiles. Building the string by concatenation is the same call.

source.work: MDN Web Docs, Object and Array constructors
source.paraphrase: The Object and Array constructors duplicate what literals already express. A single-number Array argument sets the length instead of adding an element.

invariants.why: The constructor can be less clear than a literal, but a sparse array of a requested length can be intentional.
invariants.fixHint: Write the literal. For a sized array, build it with Array.from so every slot is filled.
invariants.avoid: new Array with several elements still routes through the constructor overloads. new on another builtin is a different call and stays out of this rule.

source.paraphrase: The delete operator only removes object properties. Deleting a bare name is a silent no-op, or an error in strict and module code.

invariants.why: A delete on a plain identifier removes nothing while reading as cleanup, so the binding it names stays live and later code trusts the removal.
invariants.fixHint: Delete the property on its owner, or bind a fresh object without the key.
invariants.avoid: Deleting a computed element still deletes a property and passes. Deleting an arguments element is still flagged: accept rest parameters instead.

source.paraphrase: A label lets break and continue jump across nesting levels. The jump target sits far from the jump, so the control flow reads as goto.

invariants.why: A labeled jump exits or restarts an outer loop from deep inside, so the reader must hold every nesting level to know where execution resumes.
invariants.fixHint: Extract the labeled loop into a function and return instead of jumping to a label.
invariants.avoid: A case label inside a switch is part of the switch, not a jump target. An object key with a colon is data, not a label.

source.work: MDN Web Docs, arguments.callee and arguments.caller
source.paraphrase: The callee and caller properties expose the running function and its caller through the arguments object. Both are deprecated and forbidden in strict and module code.

invariants.why: A function that reaches itself through arguments.callee cannot be named, traced, or optimized like a plain call, and the caller link breaks as soon as the code runs strict.
invariants.fixHint: Name the function and recurse by name. For variadic input, accept rest parameters instead of reading arguments.
invariants.avoid: Reading arguments.length or an element still uses the arguments object and passes. Only the callee and caller links are flagged.
